test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 29 Aug 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Three statements are followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. You have to consider these statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the given statement.

**Statements:**

All lamps are lanterns.

All lanterns are torches.

All torches are candles.

**Conclusions:**

(i) Some candles are lamps

(II) All lanterns are lamps

(III) No lantern is a lamp

options.text: Only conclusion I and III follows

solution:
Statements:

All lamps are lanterns.

All lanterns are torches.

All torches are candles.

**Venn diagram:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aa8c2862d8cafe1c8a253fa447979ef342ec96b2d4223ce71b1473e28dee513c.png] 

**Conclusions:**

(I) Some candles are lamps → Follow → (All lamps are lanterns, all lanterns are torches & all torches are candles which means there is an indirect relation between some candles and lamps, so Some candles are lamps will be follow).

(II) All lanterns are lamps → Does not follow → (It can be possible not definite, so does not follow).

(III) No lantern is a lamp → Does not follow → (It is clearly given that all lamps are lanterns which means there are some lanterns which are definitely lamps thus the conclusion does not follow).

Thus, **only conclusion I follow**.

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 3.**
